Hi Emma — thanks for the diagram and the traffic summary; helpful. Attaching a quick sample load (sample-load.csv) and a first-draft sizing note below.

High-level sizing assumptions (interactive assistant + reranking):
- Baseline qps: 100 rps; peak ~300 rps. Average seq len 256 tokens; peak sessions up to 1k tokens (rare).
- Model footprint: using a 7B–13B family for assistant and a smaller cross-encoder for rerank. For latency/throughput tradeoffs we recommend Dedicated nodes configured as follows: 
  - Option A (balanced): 4 x A100-80GB (good for mixed throughput + memory for KV cache)
  - Option B (high-throughput): 8 x H100-80GB (if your workload needs sustained high token/s throughput)

Concurrency & queueing guidance:
- Target per-GPU concurrency: 8–16 concurrent requests (depends on model and batchability).
- Dynamic batching: aim for variable batch sizes up to 32 tokens/requests; set a short batching delay (5–10ms) to allow aggregation without hurting tail latency.
- Queue depth: configure request queue with a soft limit equal to ~2x peak per-node concurrency; enforce per-customer concurrency caps to avoid one tenant causing head-of-line latency.

Autoscaling & scaling behavior: horizontal scaling (add nodes/GPU instances) is our primary pattern for Dedicated. Scale-up time depends on your environment — in our hosted Dedicated it's usually <2 minutes for warm nodes; in private/on-prem it depends on provisioning. We also support reserve pools and burst capacity to absorb short spikes.

Routing & fallbacks:
- Use smart routing rules: prefer regional Dedicated pool, fallback to another region or to hosted model variant when capacity constrained.
- For critical interactive flows, consider a small on-hosted warm pool for immediate fallback to maintain availability.

Structured output & tool calling:
- Function-calling / structured output works with the same Dedicated runtime. We recommend validating strict JSON schema with a post-parse verifier, and enabling streaming responses with chunked validation to surface parse issues earlier.

Embeddings & rerankers:
- Keep embeddings generation on Dedicated if you need VPC/data isolation and heavy throughput. If embeddings are lower priority, you can use hosted for cost efficiency. For reranking (cross-encoder) we recommend running the cross-encoder on Dedicated when you want sub-200ms execution on small candidate sets.

Next steps I can own:
- Finalize node count + GPU mix if you can confirm expected sustained token/s (or provide a per-minute qps CSV).
- Provide a short test plan for load runs (we'll run a soak at 1.2x peak).

Attaching sample-load.csv (rough time-series). Happy to jump on the engineering call and walk through the sizing in more detail.
